title: Dispatch: olc5.12 consumed-source grant receipt + DM-visible grant provenance (user review R1/R2) (attempt 6, Sonnet)
description:
Repair attempt 6 for eshyra-olc5.12 (PR #665 @ 7d154713). It addresses the user's final review, two P2 findings: GitHub review 5559300341 on jbongaarts/eshyra#665, which `gh api repos/jbongaarts/eshyra/pulls/665/reviews` shows in full. Read `bd show eshyra-olc5.12`, especially the DESIGN RECONCILIATION note of 2026-10-17. Its rules still hold: the DM declares transitions, the engine computes clocks, and no refresh rewrites a grant's lifetime. Locate code by symbol name, because line numbers drift.

R1: CONSUMED-SOURCE GRANT HANDOFF (one-time receipt).
Problem: the real pack's magic-item:elemental-gem op `break-gem` (cost quantity:1, onDepleted destroyed) and a last-unit magic-item:feather-token `use-token` spend their unit. useItem (packages/core/src/state/itemState.ts, the `quantity === 0` and `destroyed && !deferredDestroyed` branches that call destroyInventoryItem) then deletes the inventory row. The source-faithful sequence is use_item and then start_effect with the grant. That sequence fails because validateItemGrantBinding (packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts) requires a live inventory row with a matching pack_ref.
Design (decided; do not substitute another):
 a. Add migration 0048: a new table `item_consumption_receipt(campaign_id, item_instance_id PRIMARY KEY, pack_ref NOT NULL, variant_id NULL, operation_id NOT NULL, consumed_at NOT NULL, consumed_elapsed_minutes NULL, redeemed_effect_id NULL, redeemed_at NULL, provenance, session_id)`. Follow the 0047 pattern exactly: the migration file in packages/core/data/migrations/, the schema snapshot, the legacy-adoption expectations, and whatever persistence/migrationLegacyAdoption tests enumerate migrations. Pick the campaign_id source from how useItem already scopes the instance (the owner character's campaign). If an instance has no campaign scope, write campaign_id from that same owner path and state your choice in your notes.
 b. Write the receipt ONLY in useItem's consumption path, inside its transaction, before destroyInventoryItem runs. Write it ONLY when this use destroys the row (the last unit spent, or onDepleted destroyed) AND the item's effective mechanics for the row's variant declare at least one entityGrant grant. remove_item destroyed, ammunition, item-reset destruction and the other destroyInventoryItem callers write NO receipt. Destroying an item by any other route never pays for a grant.
 c. validateItemGrantBinding: when no inventory row exists for source.itemInstanceId, look up an UNREDEEMED receipt with the same item_instance_id, the same campaign_id as the effect and pack_ref === record.key. Use the receipt's variant_id as the instance variant, so the S1 variant rules apply unchanged. If there is no receipt, a receipt already redeemed, a receipt from another campaign, or a mismatched pack_ref, refuse with distinct clear messages. A live inventory row takes precedence exactly as today.
 d. On a successful receipt bind: in the same transaction that inserts the effect, set redeemed_effect_id and redeemed_at, and write the effect's item_grant_json with sourceDestroyedAt = the receipt's consumed_at, so the binding is born tombstoned. That keeps S11 semantics: the grant ends normally and schedules no cooldown anchor, because no item survives. A second start_effect on the same receipt is refused. If the effect insert fails, the transaction rolls back, so the receipt stays unredeemed.
 e. Do NOT couple multi-unit stacks or other non-anchored spends here. That is eshyra-olc5.12.3 and stays excluded. A surviving stack binds via its live row exactly as today.
R2: DM-VISIBLE GRANT PROVENANCE.
 a. Add item_grant_json to EFFECT_COLUMNS and decode it with itemGrantColumn (packages/core/src/state/itemGrantBinding.ts). Project it in effectView (activeEffects.ts) into ActiveEffectView as an optional `itemGrant: { grantId, itemInstanceId, packRef, spellRef?, sourceDestroyedAt? }`. It is present only on grant-bound effects. This includes uncontrolled successors, which inherit the binding. Item-power effects (source_effect_ref) keep their existing representation.
 b. formatActiveEffect, which the context assembler uses in its "Active effects" section (packages/core/src/orchestrator/contextAssembler.ts), renders the grant id and the specific item instance id. When the source is tombstoned it also renders a short "source destroyed" marker. Keep the line compact. Update every exact-string expectation the change breaks, and check that each one is a format test and not a semantic guard.
 c. The start_effect tool result and listActiveEffects then carry the binding automatically. Confirm both.
PERMANENT EVIDENCE (generalized, real bundled pack; no per-example sprawl):
 - Consumption handoff: for Elemental Gem (each variant that has a grant) and a last-unit feather token with a creature grant (bird-token, if it binds as a creature; check its grant type): real use_item, then start_effect, succeeds, and the binding is tombstoned. A second start_effect on the same instance is refused. remove_item destroyed, then start_effect, is refused. A wrong campaign is refused. A wrong pack_ref is refused. start_effect on a never-existing instance id is refused. Contrast: a two-unit stack, after one use, still binds through its live row with no receipt written. A refused effect insert leaves the receipt unredeemed.
 - Provenance: two inventory instances of the same pack item and variant (two onyx-dog figurines), each bound to its own dog. listActiveEffects, and the assembled context text from the real context assembler, distinguish which instance granted which effect after a DB close and reopen (or a fresh read). After destroying one figurine, its effect shows the source-destroyed marker and the other's does not.
 - Keep all existing S1-S13 and SRD-backed deadline/anchor evidence green.
VERIFY: run the focused suites first (itemGrantSummons, activeEffects, persistence, migrationLegacyAdoption, contextAssembler, itemState), then `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack` (no pack change is expected; if one appears, stop and report), then `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing. Commit only after it exits 0.
If any decided design point conflicts with the code or source, record the precise conflict in notes, leave the bead open, and stop. Do not improvise.
notes:
Dispatched 2026-10-17 as a Claude Sonnet 5.5 Agent subagent in .worktrees/eshyra-olc5.12.13 on branch eshyra-olc5.12.13, cut from eshyra-olc5.12 @ 7d154713.
COMPLETE. Commit a79ff38e on eshyra-olc5.12.13 (not pushed). verify:dnd5e-srd-pack exit 0 (no pack change); verify:worktree exit 0: 365 files passed/2 skipped; 6948 tests passed/3 skipped.
R1: migration 0048 item_consumption_receipt (campaign_id, item_instance_id PK, pack_ref, variant_id, operation_id, consumed_at, consumed_elapsed_minutes, redeemed_effect_id, redeemed_at, provenance, session_id); schema.snapshot regenerated. Campaign scope: campaign_id = useItem input.campaignId (same scope useItem uses for attunement; inventory has no campaign column). Writer (only): useItem recordGrantConsumption(), called immediately before destroyInventoryItem at both destroy sites (quantity===0 stack path; destroyed && !deferredDestroyed state path), only if effective mechanics have >=1 entityGrant grant. remove_item/ammunition/item-reset write none. Readers: validateItemGrantBinding (activeEffects.ts; live row wins; else receipt: missing / other campaign / already redeemed / pack_ref mismatch each refused with distinct message; receipt variant used for S1 rules; anchored-cooldown economy check skipped for consumed source) and toolStartEffect.ts variant lookup (falls back to receipt variant). Redeem: redeemItemConsumptionReceipt right after the active_effect INSERT in createActiveEffect's transaction; binding born with sourceDestroyedAt=consumed_at. 
R2: item_grant_json added to EFFECT_COLUMNS/ActiveEffectRow; ActiveEffectView.itemGrant {grantId,itemInstanceId,packRef,spellRef?,sourceDestroyedAt?} via itemGrantView; formatActiveEffect renders 'item grant <id> of <instance>' plus ' (source destroyed)'. start_effect result and listActiveEffects carry it (tests confirm). start_effect tool description mentions the receipt.
Exact-string expectations updated: none broke (no existing test asserted formatted grant effects); only migration-ledger lists (migrationLegacyAdoption.test.ts: applied lists +48, ledger tail +[48,'item_consumption_receipt'], slice(-15)->(-16)) and persistence.test.ts ledger tail (47->48).
Evidence: new packages/core/test/itemGrantConsumptionReceipt.test.ts (6 tests): gem and last-unit feather token (bird-token, persistent-actor creature grant binds) use_item then start_effect succeeds, tombstoned, expires; second start refused; never-existing, wrong pack_ref, wrong campaign refused; remove_item destroyed -> refused, no receipt; refused (wrong creature) bind leaves receipt unredeemed; two onyx-dog figurines distinguishable in listActiveEffects and assembleContext/renderContextMessage, destroyed one shows source-destroyed marker, other not.
DEVIATIONS/FINDINGS (no design conflict): (1) Real-pack use_item break-gem/use-token is blocked by readiness (no clause for operation effects summon-elemental/token-kind-payload; F3/F2/F5 pending), so the test waives readiness (precedent in itemGrantSummons.test.ts, plus synthetic green effect clauses); grants/mechanics are real. (2) Gem and Feather Token are stateful (grant cooldownEconomy:quantity), so a two-unit stack is refused by use_item today; the planned 'two-unit stack binds via live row' contrast is not constructible for real items. Replaced by: refused stack use writes no receipt, and an unconsumed gem binds via live row with no receipt/no tombstone. Elemental Gem has no variants. (3) 'DB close and reopen' done as fresh reads (all state is durable columns), not a file reopen. Follow-up filed: P3 bead for stack/readiness above.
